Article 15
(1) Every family member in the fulfillment of women's rights has the obligation and responsibility to:
a. prevent the occurrence of domestic violence,
b. prevent the occurrence of divorce, and
c. provide opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural matters.
(2) The husband as head of the family together with the wife is responsible for the guidance of every family member in the fulfillment of women's rights as referred to in paragraph (1).
Paragraph on Obligations and Responsibilities of Community Organizations in the Fulfillment of Women's Rights

Article 17
(1) Every business actor in fulfilling women's rights in general has the obligations and responsibilities: a. to protect female workers from threats of violence, Discrimination, harassment, and intimidation, b. to provide job vacancies for women: c. to provide opportunities for women to be employed according to the type of work that can be performed by women,
d. to include all employees as participants in national health insurance and employment insurance in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations,
e. to comply with all applicable rules in fulfilling women's rights, and
f. to provide a lactation room.
(2) In addition to the obligations and responsibilities of business actors in general as referred to in paragraph (1), specifically:
a. every owner/manager of business in the field of industry and trade has the obligations and responsibilities:
1) not to assign female employees who are pregnant or breastfeeding to work at night: 2) to provide a lactation room: and
3) to designate certain workplaces/work rooms as smoke-free zones.
b.
every manager/owner of business in the field of hotels, lodging, homestays, guesthouses, resorts, tourist cottages, and similar accommodation places is prohibited from: 1) allowing women to stay in one room with men, unless they have a husband-wife relationship or are biological children,
2) allowing a man to visit the room of a female guest/occupant, unless they have a family relationship, 3) allowing a woman to visit the room of a male guest/occupant, unless they have a family relationship, and
4) providing massage and spa services without permission from the Regional Government. every owner/manager of entertainment and recreation venues is prohibited from providing places for the practice of prostitution or places with the potential for prostitution to occur.
(3) Every business actor/owner/manager who does not fulfill the obligations and prohibitions as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) may be subject to administrative sanctions. Administrative sanctions as referred to in paragraph (3) consist of: (4) verbal warning, written warning, administrative fine: temporary closure of business activities, or revocation of business license which is the authority of the Regional Government Administrative fine as referred to in paragraph (4) letter at most Rp50,000,000,- (fifty million

Article 32
Every person in fulfilling the rights and Protection of Children has the obligation and responsibility:
a. not to smoke near or at Children's play areas,
b. to prevent the occurrence of all forms of violence against Children,
c. not to employ Children as domestic helpers,
d. not to order children to buy cigarettes, alcoholic beverages, and other addictive substances, and
e. to prevent the occurrence of exploitation of Children.
Paragraph Obligations and Responsibilities of the Family in Fulfilling the Rights and Protection of Children Article 33 Every adult in the family in fulfilling the rights and Protection of Children has the obligation and responsibility: to prevent the occurrence of violence against Children in
a.
the family, to prevent the occurrence of exploitation of Children,
b.
to prevent the occurrence of attempts to take Children out of the house/Region for any reason without parental permission, and to report to the authorities if aware of any attempts of non-fulfillment of the rights and protection of children in the family.

Article 46
Services for women victims of violence (1) as referred to in Article 45 paragraph (3) letter constitute women who are in the condition of: women victims of the criminal act of human trafficking, women in conflict-prone and disaster areas, women workers, elderly women, women with Disabilities, women heads of Households, women victims of sexual exploitation, and/or women from other vulnerable groups.
Services for Children requiring Special Protection as referred to in Article 45 paragraph (3) letter constitute Children who are in a condition requiring Special Protection.
(2)

Article 47
The provision of services at UPTD PPA in the context of (1) Protection services for women victims of violence and for Children requiring Special Protection includes:
a. b.
d. e.
public complaints, victim outreach, case management, temporary shelter, mediation, and victim assistance.
(2) UPTD PPA in providing services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with service standards that have been established by laws and regulations. Article 48 (1) In providing Protection services for women victims of violence and for Children requiring Special Protection, UPTD PPA shall be equipped with service facilities and infrastructure in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(2) In addition to facilities and infrastructure as referred to in paragraph (1), UPTD PPA shall be equipped with human resources who will provide services for case handling.

Article 16
(1) Every community organization in the fulfillment of women's rights has the obligations and responsibilities to: a. accommodate women's representation in management, b. have programs in the field of Women's Empowerment, and c. participate in preventing violations of the fulfillment of women's rights.
(2) Every community organization that does not fulfill its obligations as referred to in paragraph (1) letter shall not be provided with services for processing registered certificates from the Regional Government.
Paragraph Obligations and Responsibilities of Business Actors in the Fulfillment of Women's Rights

Article 78
(1) Parents, religious leaders, customary leaders, youth leaders and customary law community units participate in realizing protection for women and Children by preventing the occurrence of violence against women and Children.
(2) Prevention of Violence against women and Children as referred to in paragraph (1) shall take into account local wisdom and local culture.
(3) Prevention of violence against women and Children as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be realized in the form of:
a. guiding Children to behave in accordance with religion, ethics, morals, and customs,
b. strengthening the function of houses of worship, the role of religious institutions or other religious associations,
c. supporting efforts to protect women and Children,
d. creating environmental conditions that provide a sense of security for women and Children,
e. fostering a sense of care for the Family and surrounding environment,
f. strengthening the role of customary institutions in conducting socialization on the rights of women and Children, and
g. supporting the Protection of Women and Protection of Children programs implemented by the Regional Government.

Article 35
Every community organization in the fulfillment of rights and Child Protection has the obligation and (1) responsibility:
a. to have an organizational program in the field of Child Protection: and b. to participate in providing facilities for Children who require Special Protection. Every community organization that does not fulfill (2) its obligations as referred to in paragraph (1) letter shall not be provided with services for the processing of registered certificates from the Regional Government.
Paragraph Obligations and Responsibilities of Business Actors in the Fulfillment of Rights and Child Protection

Article 49
UPTD PPA in providing protection services to women victims of violence and for Children who require Special Protection coordinates with: a. hospitals, community health centers and other health service facilities,
b. correctional centers,
c. sector police, d. resort police,
e. regional police,
f. district prosecutor's office,
g. high prosecutor's office, h. district courts and high courts,
i. service centers for placement and protection of Indonesian workers,
j. regional office of the Ministry of Religious Affairs,
k. regional office of the Ministry of Law,
l. special correctional institutions for Children, and/or
m. social welfare organizing institutions. Article 50 In addition to coordination as referred to in Article 49, UPTD PPA may coordinate with Village Governments and the Provincial Government of West Sumatra.

Article 45
The Regional Government is responsible for providing (1) protection services for women victims of violence and Special Protection for Children.
Protection services for women victims of violence and (2) Special Protection for Children as referred to in paragraph (1) are located at the UPTD PPA.
The provision of services as referred to in paragraph (1) (3) includes:
a. follow-up referral services for women victims of violence requiring coordination at the Regional level: and b. Special Protection for Children services requiring coordination at the Regional level.
The establishment of UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (4) (2) is stipulated by Regent Regulation in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

CHAPTER III
PROTECTION OF WOMEN
Part One Rights and Obligations of Women
Article 11
Every woman has the right to:
a. b.
obtain respect for her worth and dignity as a human being, obtain decent work in accordance with her worth, dignity and capability,
c. obtain special rights in relation to her reproductive function personally and/or in the workplace, d. obtain protection from physical, psychological, sexual violence, and neglect,
e. obtain identity and marital status, f. obtain education at every type and level of education, obtain freedom in the public and political sphere, obtain protection from economic exploitation and sexual exploitation, and
i. obtain protection from acts of Discrimination. Article 12 (1) Every woman has the obligation to:
a. uphold religious values and customary values, b. maintain morals, honor, decency, ethics, and behavior in family and community life, and a. mutually respect, mutually love and help one another with all Family members and relatives.
(2) Every woman in a marriage bond has the obligation to carry out obligations as a wife and/or mother, care for and educate Children together with her husband in accordance with religious norms, customs, and laws and regulations.

ARTICLE BY ARTICLE
Il.
Article Sufficiently clear. Article Letter What is meant by respect for human rights is the principle that underlies efforts in carrying out the protection and empowerment of women and children based on respect, protection and advancement of human rights as stipulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Letter What is meant by non-discrimination is the principle that underlies the regulation and implementation of protection for women and children without differentiating treatment, actions or policies based on background, ethnicity, religion, race, class, ethnic group, culture, language, gender and physical and/or mental condition. Letter What is meant by justice and gender equality is a condition where women and men enjoy equal status and have equal conditions to fully realize their human rights and potential for the integrity and continuity of the household proportionally. Letter What is meant by the best interests of women and children is all efforts to realize protection that is directed towards the best possible efforts and services in accordance with existing capabilities and potential by considering the survival and development of women and children. Letter What is meant by victim protection is the principle in regulating the protection of women and children aimed at protecting the rights and interests of victims who experience various forms of violence, discrimination, mistreatment, exploitation, neglect, trafficking and various other forms of criminal acts. Letter What is meant by "Togetherness" is a principle that encourages the role of all stakeholders to jointly make efforts to protect women and children to realize common welfare. GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of public welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.
The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare while always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled. Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or seized by anyone. In the context of Upholding Human Rights (HAM) to guarantee justice for every individual, efforts are made to prevent all forms of unbalanced treatment or treatment deemed detrimental to other parties, whether between individuals, between groups of individuals, or between individuals as well as between government and society, including the process of marginalization of women which causes women to be vulnerable to acts of violence, discrimination and exploitation in both domestic and public spheres.
On one side, women's empowerment efforts aim to eliminate all forms of discrimination and gender stereotypes, ensure women have equal access to education, health, economy, and political participation. This is important to optimize the role of women as agents of change and significant contributors to regional progress. On the other side, child protection becomes an essential foundation to ensure every child grows and develops optimally, free from violence, exploitation, neglect, and discrimination, so that they can become quality and competitive future generations.
Women's empowerment and child protection are implemented in order to realize gender equality and justice. To implement these affairs, efforts are needed to increase the capacity of women's resources and strengthen gender mainstreaming institutions, through gender mainstreaming strategies and gender-disaggregated data. This Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is a concrete manifestation of the commitment of the Regional Government of Mentawai Islands Regency in creating a just, equal, and prosperous society, where every individual, regardless of gender and age, can feel and enjoy their basic rights fully. This Perda is formed as a response to social realities that show that women and children, as vulnerable groups, still often face various challenges and obstacles in accessing their rights and actively participating in development.
With the existence of this Perda, it is expected that a strong legal framework will be created, a coordinated institutional system, as well as directed and sustainable programs in efforts to empower women and protect children throughout the Mentawai Islands Regency.

ABOUT
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION
GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of public welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.
The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare while always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled. Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or seized by anyone. In the context of Upholding Human Rights (HAM) to guarantee justice for every individual, efforts are made to prevent all forms of unbalanced treatment or treatment deemed detrimental to other parties, whether between individuals, between groups of individuals, or between individuals as well as between government and society, including the process of marginalization of women which causes women to be vulnerable to acts of violence, discrimination and exploitation in both domestic and public spheres.
On one side, women's empowerment efforts aim to eliminate all forms of discrimination and gender stereotypes, ensure women have equal access to education, health, economy, and political participation. This is important to optimize the role of women as agents of change and significant contributors to regional progress. On the other side, child protection becomes an essential foundation to ensure every child grows and develops optimally, free from violence, exploitation, neglect, and discrimination, so that they can become quality and competitive future generations.
Women's empowerment and child protection are implemented in order to realize gender equality and justice. To implement these affairs, efforts are needed to increase the capacity of women's resources and strengthen gender mainstreaming institutions, through gender mainstreaming strategies and gender-disaggregated data. This Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is a concrete manifestation of the commitment of the Regional Government of Mentawai Islands Regency in creating a just, equal, and prosperous society, where every individual, regardless of gender and age, can feel and enjoy their basic rights fully. This Perda is formed as a response to social realities that show that women and children, as vulnerable groups, still often face various challenges and obstacles in accessing their rights and actively participating in development.
With the existence of this Perda, it is expected that a strong legal framework will be created, a coordinated institutional system, as well as directed and sustainable programs in efforts to empower women and protect children throughout the Mentawai Islands Regency.

ABOUT
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION
GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of public welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.
The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare while always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled. Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or seized by anyone. In the context of Upholding Human Rights (HAM) to guarantee justice for every individual, efforts are made to prevent all forms of unbalanced treatment or treatment deemed detrimental to other parties, whether between individuals, between groups of individuals, or between individuals as well as between government and society, including the process of marginalization of women which causes women to be vulnerable to acts of violence, discrimination and exploitation in both domestic and public spheres.
On one side, women's empowerment efforts aim to eliminate all forms of discrimination and gender stereotypes, ensure women have equal access to education, health, economy, and political participation. This is important to optimize the role of women as agents of change and significant contributors to regional progress. On the other side, child protection becomes an essential foundation to ensure every child grows and develops optimally, free from violence, exploitation, neglect, and discrimination, so that they can become quality and competitive future generations.
Women's empowerment and child protection are implemented in order to realize gender equality and justice. To implement these affairs, efforts are needed to increase the capacity of women's resources and strengthen gender mainstreaming institutions, through gender mainstreaming strategies and gender-disaggregated data. This Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is a concrete manifestation of the commitment of the Regional Government of Mentawai Islands Regency in creating a just, equal, and prosperous society, where every individual, regardless of gender and age, can feel and enjoy their basic rights fully. This Perda is formed as a response to social realities that show that women and children, as vulnerable groups, still often face various challenges and obstacles in accessing their rights and actively participating in development.
With the existence of this Perda, it is expected that a strong legal framework will be created, a coordinated institutional system, as well as directed and sustainable programs in efforts to empower women and protect children throughout the Mentawai Islands Regency.

ABOUT
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION
GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of public welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.
The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare while always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled. Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or seized by anyone. In the context of Upholding Human Rights (HAM) to guarantee justice for every individual, efforts are made to prevent all forms of unbalanced treatment or treatment deemed detrimental to other parties, whether between individuals, between groups of individuals, or between individuals as well as between government and society, including the process of marginalization of women which causes women to be vulnerable to acts of violence, discrimination and exploitation in both domestic and public spheres.
On one side, women's empowerment efforts aim to eliminate all forms of discrimination and gender stereotypes, ensure women have equal access to education, health, economy, and political participation. This is important to optimize the role of women as agents of change and significant contributors to regional progress. On the other side, child protection becomes an essential foundation to ensure every child grows and develops optimally, free from violence, exploitation, neglect, and discrimination, so that they can become quality and competitive future generations.
Women's empowerment and child protection are implemented in order to realize gender equality and justice. To implement these affairs, efforts are needed to increase the capacity of women's resources and strengthen gender mainstreaming institutions, through gender mainstreaming strategies and gender-disaggregated data. This Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is a concrete manifestation of the commitment of the Regional Government of Mentawai Islands Regency in creating a just, equal, and prosperous society, where every individual, regardless of gender and age, can feel and enjoy their basic rights fully. This Perda is formed as a response to social realities that show that women and children, as vulnerable groups, still often face various challenges and obstacles in accessing their rights and actively participating in development.
With the existence of this Perda, it is expected that a strong legal framework will be created, a coordinated institutional system, as well as directed and sustainable programs in efforts to empower women and protect children throughout the Mentawai Islands Regency.

ABOUT
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION
GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of public welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.
The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare while always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled. Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or seized by anyone. In the context of Upholding Human Rights (HAM) to guarantee justice for every individual, efforts are made to prevent all forms of unbalanced treatment or treatment deemed detrimental to other parties, whether between individuals, between groups of individuals, or between individuals as well as between government and society, including the process of marginalization of women which causes women to be vulnerable to acts of violence, discrimination and exploitation in both domestic and public spheres.
On one side, women's empowerment efforts aim to eliminate all forms of discrimination and gender stereotypes, ensure women have equal access to education, health, economy, and political participation. This is important to optimize the role of women as agents of change and significant contributors to regional progress. On the other side, child protection becomes an essential foundation to ensure every child grows and develops optimally, free from violence, exploitation, neglect, and discrimination, so that they can become quality and competitive future generations.
Women's empowerment and child protection are implemented in order to realize gender equality and justice. To implement these affairs, efforts are needed to increase the capacity of women's resources and strengthen gender mainstreaming institutions, through gender mainstreaming strategies and gender-disaggregated data. This Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is a concrete manifestation of the commitment of the Regional Government of Mentawai Islands Regency in creating a just, equal, and prosperous society, where every individual, regardless of gender and age, can feel and enjoy their basic rights fully. This Perda is formed as a response to social realities that show that women and children, as vulnerable groups, still often face various challenges and obstacles in accessing their rights and actively participating in development.
With the existence of this Perda, it is expected that a strong legal framework will be created, a coordinated institutional system, as well as directed and sustainable programs in efforts to empower women and protect children throughout the Mentawai Islands Regency.

(1) The Village Government in fulfilling women's rights has the obligations and responsibilities to:
a. formulate policies in the field of women's empowerment at the Village level,

d. compile data profiles of women at the Village level,

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION
GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of public welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.
The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare while always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled. Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or seized by anyone. In the context of Upholding Human Rights (HAM) to guarantee justice for every individual, efforts are made to prevent all forms of unbalanced treatment or treatment deemed detrimental to other parties, whether between individuals, between groups of individuals, or between individuals as well as between government and society, including the process of marginalization of women which causes women to be vulnerable to acts of violence, discrimination and exploitation in both domestic and public spheres.
On one side, women's empowerment efforts aim to eliminate all forms of discrimination and gender stereotypes, ensure women have equal access to education, health, economy, and political participation. This is important to optimize the role of women as agents of change and significant contributors to regional progress. On the other side, child protection becomes an essential foundation to ensure every child grows and develops optimally, free from violence, exploitation, neglect, and discrimination, so that they can become quality and competitive future generations.
Women's empowerment and child protection are implemented in order to realize gender equality and justice. To implement these affairs, efforts are needed to increase the capacity of women's resources and strengthen gender mainstreaming institutions, through gender mainstreaming strategies and gender-disaggregated data. This Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is a concrete manifestation of the commitment of the Regional Government of Mentawai Islands Regency in creating a just, equal, and prosperous society, where every individual, regardless of gender and age, can feel and enjoy their basic rights fully. This Perda is formed as a response to social realities that show that women and children, as vulnerable groups, still often face various challenges and obstacles in accessing their rights and actively participating in development.
With the existence of this Perda, it is expected that a strong legal framework will be created, a coordinated institutional system, as well as directed and sustainable programs in efforts to empower women and protect children throughout the Mentawai Islands Regency.

Article The regulation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is based on: a. respect for human rights,
b. non-discrimination: c. justice and Gender Equality:
d. best interests of women and children, e. protection of victims, and
f. togetherness.
Article The objectives of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection are: a. to improve the quality of life of women, children, and Family quality,
b. to increase the institutional capacity of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in the Region, including the development of Gender and Child data systems, and
c. to provide protection of women's rights and fulfillment of children's rights including Special Protection for children from various forms of violence and other discriminatory treatment. Article The scope of this Regional Regulation includes:
a. Women's Empowerment:
b. implementation of Child Protection, c. protection services for women victims of violence and Special Protection for Children, improvement of Family quality, strengthening and improvement of institutions, cooperation, community participation, guidance and supervision, sanctions, and closing.

Article The objectives of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection are: a. to improve the quality of life of women, children, and Family quality,
b. to increase the institutional capacity of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in the Region, including the development of Gender and Child data systems, and
c. to provide protection of women's rights and fulfillment of children's rights including Special Protection for children from various forms of violence and other discriminatory treatment. Article The scope of this Regional Regulation includes:
a. Women's Empowerment:

ABOUT
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION
GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of public welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.
The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare while always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled. Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or seized by anyone. In the context of Upholding Human Rights (HAM) to guarantee justice for every individual, efforts are made to prevent all forms of unbalanced treatment or treatment deemed detrimental to other parties, whether between individuals, between groups of individuals, or between individuals as well as between government and society, including the process of marginalization of women which causes women to be vulnerable to acts of violence, discrimination and exploitation in both domestic and public spheres.
On one side, women's empowerment efforts aim to eliminate all forms of discrimination and gender stereotypes, ensure women have equal access to education, health, economy, and political participation. This is important to optimize the role of women as agents of change and significant contributors to regional progress. On the other side, child protection becomes an essential foundation to ensure every child grows and develops optimally, free from violence, exploitation, neglect, and discrimination, so that they can become quality and competitive future generations.
Women's empowerment and child protection are implemented in order to realize gender equality and justice. To implement these affairs, efforts are needed to increase the capacity of women's resources and strengthen gender mainstreaming institutions, through gender mainstreaming strategies and gender-disaggregated data. This Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is a concrete manifestation of the commitment of the Regional Government of Mentawai Islands Regency in creating a just, equal, and prosperous society, where every individual, regardless of gender and age, can feel and enjoy their basic rights fully. This Perda is formed as a response to social realities that show that women and children, as vulnerable groups, still often face various challenges and obstacles in accessing their rights and actively participating in development.
With the existence of this Perda, it is expected that a strong legal framework will be created, a coordinated institutional system, as well as directed and sustainable programs in efforts to empower women and protect children throughout the Mentawai Islands Regency.

GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of public welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or seized by anyone. ABOUT
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION
GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of public welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.
The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare while always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled. Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or seized by anyone. In the context of Upholding Human Rights (HAM) to guarantee justice for every individual, efforts are made to prevent all forms of unbalanced treatment or treatment deemed detrimental to other parties, whether between individuals, between groups of individuals, or between individuals as well as between government and society, including the process of marginalization of women which causes women to be vulnerable to acts of violence, discrimination and exploitation in both domestic and public spheres.
On one side, women's empowerment efforts aim to eliminate all forms of discrimination and gender stereotypes, ensure women have equal access to education, health, economy, and political participation. This is important to optimize the role of women as agents of change and significant contributors to regional progress. On the other side, child protection becomes an essential foundation to ensure every child grows and develops optimally, free from violence, exploitation, neglect, and discrimination, so that they can become quality and competitive future generations.
Women's empowerment and child protection are implemented in order to realize gender equality and justice. To implement these affairs, efforts are needed to increase the capacity of women's resources and strengthen gender mainstreaming institutions, through gender mainstreaming strategies and gender-disaggregated data. This Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is a concrete manifestation of the commitment of the Regional Government of Mentawai Islands Regency in creating a just, equal, and prosperous society, where every individual, regardless of gender and age, can feel and enjoy their basic rights fully. This Perda is formed as a response to social realities that show that women and children, as vulnerable groups, still often face various challenges and obstacles in accessing their rights and actively participating in development.
With the existence of this Perda, it is expected that a strong legal framework will be created, a coordinated institutional system, as well as directed and sustainable programs in efforts to empower women and protect children throughout the Mentawai Islands Regency.

GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of public welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.
The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare while always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled. Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or seized by anyone. In the context of Upholding Human Rights (HAM) to guarantee justice for every individual, efforts are made to prevent all forms of unbalanced treatment or treatment deemed detrimental to other parties, whether between individuals, between groups of individuals, or between individuals as well as between government and society, including the process of marginalization of women which causes women to be vulnerable to acts of violence, discrimination and exploitation in both domestic and public spheres.
On one side, women's empowerment efforts aim to eliminate all forms of discrimination and gender stereotypes, ensure women have equal access to education, health, economy, and political participation. This is important to optimize the role of women as agents of change and significant contributors to regional progress. On the other side, child protection becomes an essential foundation to ensure every child grows and develops optimally, free from violence, exploitation, neglect, and discrimination, so that they can become quality and competitive future generations.
Women's empowerment and child protection are implemented in order to realize gender equality and justice. To implement these affairs, efforts are needed to increase the capacity of women's resources and strengthen gender mainstreaming institutions, through gender mainstreaming strategies and gender-disaggregated data. This Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is a concrete manifestation of the commitment of the Regional Government of Mentawai Islands Regency in creating a just, equal, and prosperous society, where every individual, regardless of gender and age, can feel and enjoy their basic rights fully. This Perda is formed as a response to social realities that show that women and children, as vulnerable groups, still often face various challenges and obstacles in accessing their rights and actively participating in development.
With the existence of this Perda, it is expected that a strong legal framework will be created, a coordinated institutional system, as well as directed and sustainable programs in efforts to empower women and protect children throughout the Mentawai Islands Regency.

ABOUT
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION
GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of public welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.
The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare while always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled. Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or seized by anyone. In the context of Upholding Human Rights (HAM) to guarantee justice for every individual, efforts are made to prevent all forms of unbalanced treatment or treatment deemed detrimental to other parties, whether between individuals, between groups of individuals, or between individuals as well as between government and society, including the process of marginalization of women which causes women to be vulnerable to acts of violence, discrimination and exploitation in both domestic and public spheres.
On one side, women's empowerment efforts aim to eliminate all forms of discrimination and gender stereotypes, ensure women have equal access to education, health, economy, and political participation. This is important to optimize the role of women as agents of change and significant contributors to regional progress. On the other side, child protection becomes an essential foundation to ensure every child grows and develops optimally, free from violence, exploitation, neglect, and discrimination, so that they can become quality and competitive future generations.
Women's empowerment and child protection are implemented in order to realize gender equality and justice. To implement these affairs, efforts are needed to increase the capacity of women's resources and strengthen gender mainstreaming institutions, through gender mainstreaming strategies and gender-disaggregated data. This Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is a concrete manifestation of the commitment of the Regional Government of Mentawai Islands Regency in creating a just, equal, and prosperous society, where every individual, regardless of gender and age, can feel and enjoy their basic rights fully. This Perda is formed as a response to social realities that show that women and children, as vulnerable groups, still often face various challenges and obstacles in accessing their rights and actively participating in development.
With the existence of this Perda, it is expected that a strong legal framework will be created, a coordinated institutional system, as well as directed and sustainable programs in efforts to empower women and protect children throughout the Mentawai Islands Regency.

Article 37
The Village Government in the fulfillment of rights and Child Protection has the obligations and responsibilities: (1)
a. formulating policies in the field of Child Protection, b. facilitating the establishment of Child organizations at the village level,
c. providing budget to support activities for the fulfillment of rights and Protection of Child victims of violence as well as Children requiring Special Protection at the Village level, d. compiling profile data of Children at the Village level,
e. implementing the implementation of Child-friendly Village in programs and activities of the village revenue and expenditure budget,
f. providing education scholarship budget for underprivileged Children,
g. providing budget for Integrated Service Posts (Posyandu) at the Village level, h. providing budget for Early Childhood Education management institutions, preventing the occurrence of violence and exploitation of Children, 1.
j. preventing attempts to take Children out of the Village/Region without parental permission and the knowledge of the Village Head, and k. making efforts to fulfill the rights of Children requiring Special Protection.

d. compile data profiles of women at the Village level,
e. implement the implementation of women-friendly and Child-caring Villages in programs and activities of the village revenue and expenditure budget,
f. increase women's representation in the structure of Village apparatus, membership of the Village Consultative Body, and management of Village customary institutions,

CLOSING PROVISIONS

The Implementing Regulations of this Regional Regulation must be stipulated no later than (one) year calculated from the promulgation of this Regional Regulation.

The Regional level Puspa Forum in carrying out the task of (1) coordinating as referred to in Article 74 paragraph (1) is conducted in the form of:
a. Regional level coordination, b. sectoral coordination, and
c. special coordination.
Regional level coordination as referred to in (2) paragraph (1) letter a is implemented at least (one) time in (one) year or at any time when necessary to strengthen communication, cooperation, and discuss the implementation of the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection sector at the Regional level. Sectoral coordination as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is implemented periodically at least (one) time in (four) months or at any time when (3) necessary to discuss program activities that are its duties.

Article 39
Regional Government in the effort to fulfill the rights and Protection of Children has the obligations and responsibilities:
a. to formulate short, medium, and long-term strategic plans for Child Protection, b. to provide legal aid facilities in the form of advocacy and assistance for victims and or families of victims of violence against Children, c. to encourage the responsibility of all stakeholders to fulfill obligations and responsibilities in fulfilling the rights and Protection of Children, d. to provide budget for programs for the fulfillment of rights and Protection of Children at the Regional level,
e. to facilitate the establishment of children's organizations at the Regional level,
f. to provide shelter facilities for child victims of violence, and
g. to coordinate the implementation of the fulfillment of rights and Protection of Children in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 78
(1) Parents, religious leaders, customary leaders, youth leaders and customary law community units participate in realizing protection for women and Children by preventing the occurrence of violence against women and Children.
(2) Prevention of Violence against women and Children as referred to in paragraph (1) shall take into account local wisdom and local culture.
(3) Prevention of violence against women and Children as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be realized in the form of:
a. guiding Children to behave in accordance with religion, ethics, morals, and customs,
b. strengthening the function of houses of worship, the role of religious institutions or other religious associations,
c. supporting efforts to protect women and Children,
d. creating environmental conditions that provide a sense of security for women and Children,
e. fostering a sense of care for the Family and surrounding environment,
f. strengthening the role of customary institutions in conducting socialization on the rights of women and Children, and
g. supporting the Protection of Women and Protection of Children programs implemented by the Regional Government.

Article 21
The Regional Government in efforts for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection has the obligations and responsibilities:
a. to formulate short, medium, and long-term strategic plans for women's protection:
b. to provide legal aid facilities in the form of advocacy and assistance for victims and or families of victims of violence against women,

g. to facilitate the establishment of women's organizations at the Regional level:
h. to provide shelter facilities for victims of violence:

(1) In carrying out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in Article 21, the Regent forms an integrated team.
